previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain similar to prior pancreatitis episodes, but with normal lipase levels and only mild CT findings. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control, then gradually advanced to a solid diet. A UTI was treated with a 3-day course of levofloxacin. EGD and capsule endoscopy revealed chronic duodenitis, suggesting possible small bowel disease or IBD, though the etiology remained unclear. A colonoscopy was attempted but unsuccessful due to inadequate bowel prep, requiring a future repeat with full GoLytely preparation. Her orthostatic hypotension was managed with dose adjustments to fludrocortisone and betaxolol, and she was discharged home in good condition, tolerating oral intake and requiring no IV medications.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Known cystic lesion of the pancreas and prior episodes of
pancreatitis, please evaluate for flow through the main pancreatic duct.

COMPARISON:  MRCP of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired through the
abdomen on a 1.5 Tesla magnet, including dynamic high-resolution 3D imaging
obtained prior to, during, and after the uneventful intravenous administration
of 0.1 mmol/kg (15 mL) of gadolinium-DTPA.  Thick-slab SSFSE images were
obtained through the pancreatic duct prior to and following the intravenous
administration of 13.5 mcg of secretin at 30 second intervals for 10 minutes.

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reformatted and subtraction images were generated and
reviewed on a separate workstation.

FINDINGS:  Again seen in the tail of the pancreas are two small cystic
lesions, measuring 8 x 8 mm (100:55, 8:20) and 4-mm (8:19; 100:60), both of
which display homogeneous T2 hyperintensity and lack enhancement after the
administration of gadolinium and which are unchanged in size.  The pancreatic
duct is nondilated.  Following the administration of secretin, there is
transient dilation of the duct with prompt return to pre-secretin caliber, and
marked secretion of fluid into the duodenum with prompt transit beyond the
ligament of Treitz.  The pancreatic parenchyma enhances homogeneously without
evidence of solid enhancing masses.

The mild irregularity of the intrahepatic bile ducts which was noted on the
previous study is less apparent on today's study, and several foci of patchy
T2 hyperintensity previously present in the hepatic parenchyma are no longer
visualized.  No enhancing hepatic masses are identified.  The portal vein is
patent.  The gallbladder is nondistended.

The spleen and adrenal glands appear unremarkable.  No renal masses or
hydronephrosis are present.  There are no pathologically enlarged mesenteric
or retroperitoneal lymph nodes.  The imaged loops of small bowel appear within
normal limits.

The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber.  Although mild irregularity of the
celiac axis is again noted, this finding may be artifactual and appears
unchanged.

The imaged marrow signal appears within normal limits.

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reformations and subtraction images were essential in
delineating the above-described findings.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No interval change in two cystic lesions of the pancreatic tail up to 8 mm
in diameter.
2.  Normal secretin examination of the pancreas.
3.  Previously noted irregularity of the biliary ducts is no longer apparent
on today's examination, although attention on further followup imaging is
recommended.
